caption: A scalar threads through nested lists
Outer builds every pairing of the two lists' elements
Prepend with a list adds it as one element, not spliced
Flatten removes the nesting and joins the rows
Map applies a symbolic head to each element

expr: [Solve, [List, [Equal, [Add, x, [Multiply, -1, y]], 1], [Equal, [Add, x, y], 0]], x, y]
epsil.back: [Solve, [List, [Equal, [Subtract, x, y], 1], [Equal, [Add, x, y], 0]], x, y]

wolfram.note: Emit: Map(f, list, levelspec) goes to MapThread[f, {list, {2}}], which errors in Wolfram (MapThread::mptc, dimensions 3 and 1), whose Map[f, list, {2}] is {{f[1], f[2]}, {f[3], f[4]}, {f[5], f[6]}}. Ours answers {f({1, 2}, 2)}, so it has no level-spec reading of Map either.
